rules.title: static IV/nonce
rules.why_flagged: IV, nonce, salt or counter identifier at a site where it may be fixed
rules.flag_condition: candidate when the value is assigned from a literal array, declared static/const/global, when an EVP_*Init call's 5th argument is not random, or when a GCM mode is used with a fixed nonce

rules.title: weak primitive
rules.why_flagged: broken or deprecated cryptographic primitive, or ECB mode
rules.flag_condition: candidate wherever the primitive is used for a security purpose. The (_|\b) tail is deliberate: \b alone misses DES_encrypt. The ECB branch is case-insensitive and does not rely on \b, because \bECB\b matches neither EVP_aes_128_ecb (lowercase, and _ is a word character so there is no boundary) nor MODE_ECB. The DES branch stays case-sensitive because des is a common C name for a destination; Java's "DESede" and "SHA-1" and the lowercase OpenSSL cipher names Node, Ruby and PHP pass (des-ede3-cbc, des-cbc) have branches of their own

rules.title: key size
rules.why_flagged: key, parameter or work factor below the current floor
rules.flag_condition: candidate for the literal key sizes matched, for symmetric key buffers declared [5]..[8] bytes, for PBKDF iteration counts below 100000, and for bcrypt cost below 10. The last two are numeric comparisons the pattern cannot make: the PBKDF/bcrypt branch surfaces the site and the validator reads the number

rules.title: TLS verification
rules.why_flagged: peer verification is disabled, or its result is not consumed
rules.flag_condition: candidate when verification is switched off, when X509_verify_cert's result is discarded, when SSL_get_verify_result is unused, when a TrustManager's checkServerTrusted is empty, or when a hostname verifier or certificate-validation callback accepts every peer. The language-level switches (rejectUnauthorized: false, ssl.CERT_NONE, check_hostname = False, VERIFY_NONE, danger_accept_invalid_certs, a PHP 'verify' => false) are the same defect spelled per library

rules.title: attacker-controlled comparison length
rules.why_flagged: comparison whose length is a variable, or which compares against a secret
rules.flag_condition: candidate when the length argument is a variable, when strlen() of attacker-controlled input supplies the compare length, or when strcmp compares against a secret, token, hash, signature or password
